options.text: $1$ is neither prime nor composite because it has only one factor.
Call $1$ a composite number from the label composite alone.
$17$ is prime (exactly two factors) and $8$ is composite (more than two factors).
The prime and composite labels are produced by a jump-size treasure hunt on a number line, not by these factor lists.

stem:
Vikram lists the factors of three whole numbers: $1$ has only $\{1\}$; $17$ has $\{1,17\}$; $8$ has $\{1,2,4,8\}$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims classify $1$, $17$, and $8$ correctly?

teacher.key_rationale: 1 has one factor so is neither; 17 has exactly two factors so is prime; 8 has more than two factors so is composite. A and C state that. B mislabels 1 as composite. D swaps in a number-line jump mechanism instead of factor counts.
